 Page Industries Q2 revenue rises 11.5 per cent as higher costs squeeze margins
 Jockey maker’s sales reach Rs 14,396 million, but EBITDA margin falls 80 basis points amid input cost pressures
 Published
 17 hours ago on
 November 12, 2026 
 By
 indiantelevision.com Team 
 Follow us on Google News 
 Follow us on WhatsApp 
 Share 
 Tweet 
 MUMBAI: Page Industries has kept its double-digit revenue growth run going, but rising costs and relatively modest volume expansion have taken some shine off its second-quarter performance.
 The maker of Jockey and Speedo products reported revenue from operations of Rs 14,396 million ($153.3 million) for the quarter ended 30 September 2026, up 11.5 per cent year-on-year. Revenue was also 1.4 per cent higher than the Rs 14,204 million reported in the first quarter of FY27.
 However, operating profit grew more slowly than sales. Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) increased 7.4 per cent to Rs 3,001 million, taking the EBITDA margin down 80 basis points to 20.8 per cent from 21.7 per cent a year earlier. The margin improved from 20.3 per cent in the preceding quarter.
 A closer look at the numbers shows that higher realisations contributed significantly to revenue growth. Sales volume increased 5.5 per cent year-on-year to 59.7 million pieces, while implied average realisation per piece rose 5.7 per cent to Rs 241.1.
 The volume figure, however, was 3.7 per cent lower than the 62 million pieces sold in Q1 FY27. The improvement in realisations reflects the impact of a price increase introduced in the first quarter, along with a richer product mix that included new Disney and Marvel ranges and athleisure offerings.
 Operating costs, excluding depreciation and amortisation, rose 12.7 per cent year-on-year to Rs 11,395 million, outpacing revenue growth. Raw material expenses increased around 11 per cent to approximately Rs 3,600 million, with cotton price volatility and elevated crude-linked synthetic fibre costs adding to the pressure.
 The impact extended beyond operating earnings. Depreciation and finance costs, net of other income, increased to Rs 291 million from Rs 184 million in the year-ago quarter. Other income fell 30 per cent to Rs 135.8 million.
 Profit before tax rose 3.8 per cent to Rs 2,710 million, while profit after tax increased 4 per cent to Rs 2,025 million. The net profit margin narrowed by 102 basis points to 14.1 per cent from 15.1 per cent in Q2 FY26.
 For media and advertising watchers, Page Industries’ quarterly filing and investor presentation do not provide a separate figure for advertisement and marketing expenditure.
 The company highlighted digital campaigns across Instagram, Facebook and YouTube for Jockey and Speedo. However, the exact advertising outlay is not separately disclosed and remains part of broader operating expenses.
 For the first half of FY27, revenue grew 9.7 per cent year-on-year to Rs 28,601 million, supported by sales of 121.7 million pieces, up 5.6 per cent.
 EBITDA increased 2.6 per cent to Rs 5,891 million, while the margin declined 142 basis points to 20.6 per cent. Profit after tax was largely flat at Rs 3,954 million, compared with Rs 3,956 million in the first half of FY26.
 The half-year figures underline the pressure on profitability, with operating costs rising 11.7 per cent to Rs 22,710 million, faster than revenue.
 Page Industries continues to expand its retail reach. Jockey is available across 1,14,591 multi-brand retail outlets and 1,626 exclusive brand stores in 2,722 cities and towns. The brand is also present on quick-commerce platforms including Blinkit and Swiggy Instamart.
 Speedo has a presence in 835 multi-brand stores and 36 exclusive outlets. The company reported an annualised return on capital employed of 73.8 per cent.
 The board declared a second interim dividend of Rs 150 per share, taking the total dividend declared for FY27 so far to Rs 350 per share.
 Managing director V.S. Ganesh said profitability remained within the company’s planned range despite persistent pressure from cotton prices. He also pointed to an SAP S/4HANA rollout scheduled for the fourth quarter and a new fulfilment hub in West Bengal as initiatives expected to improve operational efficiency.
 The market response was less encouraging. Page Industries shares fell nearly 13 per cent to Rs 31,850 on the results day, as investors reacted to slower volume growth and the contraction in operating margins.
